title: ICE Officer Shoots and Wounds Venezuelan DoorDash Driver in North Austin
detail: An ICE officer shot and wounded Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan national, in North Austin, Texas just before 1 p.m. on Sunday, September 20, 2026, near Anderson Square on Research Boulevard. Garces Perez was delivering food for DoorDash — the company confirmed he was actively on a delivery — when ICE officers conducting a targeted enforcement operation based on license-plate checks approached his vehicle. He was shot once in the torso and transported to Dell Seton Medical Center within nine minutes, listed in serious but stable condition; a bullet remained lodged in his back as of Monday. DHS said Garces Perez was an undocumented immigrant with a final order of removal, while his attorney disputed that characterization, saying he has no criminal history, has lived in Austin about two years, is married to a woman with legal U.S. status, and had no final removal order. He was released from the hospital into federal custody Sunday evening and was being held at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall by Monday. Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis confirmed local police were not involved in the operation. About 100 protesters gathered at the scene. Mayor Kirk Watson said he was 'very angry and extremely disappointed' and 'not surprised' given a pattern of similar incidents in other cities. The shooting is at least the third involving federal immigration agents in Texas since the start of Trump's second term, following the fatal July 7, 2026 shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a Houston traffic stop. Reporting Sept. 22–23 revealed the officer who fired was not wearing a body camera despite having been issued one — DHS Secretary Mullin had said in August all agents would be equipped by the end of August — and DHS did not explain the gap; a second officer at the scene had a body camera, but its footage does not capture the shooting itself. Garces Perez was transferred back to hospital Monday over numbness on his left side and the still-lodged bullet, his attorney saying he received only Tylenol and ibuprofen for pain; he remains held at the South Texas Detention Complex in Pearsall, and a federal judge has ordered an in-person hearing on September 30 while blocking his deportation until then.

title: ICE Agents Mistakenly Detain and Injure US Citizen in Evanston, Illinois Suburb of Chicago
detail: ICE agents in Evanston, Illinois — a Chicago suburb — mistakenly detained a Black man they believed matched someone they were targeting on Sunday morning, September 20, 2026, around 9:49 a.m. Cellphone video from a witness showed the man pinned to the ground, saying 'I'm a f***ing US citizen,' with a witness describing agents as 'being rough with him' and saying one appeared to strike him in the face. He sustained injuries to his head, neck, and teeth; Evanston's police chief met with him at a local hospital, where an evidence technician photographed and documented his injuries. ICE said agents 'immediately identified themselves as law enforcement' and gave 'lawful commands' but that the man 'was not cooperative and refused to identify himself,' and that officers 'relied on their training.' Agents ultimately determined he was not their target, confirmed he was a U.S. citizen, and released him. Evanston police said they are investigating and preserving body-camera footage from the scene.

title: Guatemalan Man Dies After Fleeing Attempted ICE Traffic Stop in Grand Rapids, Michigan
detail: Mario David Coronado Juárez, a 36-year-old undocumented Guatemalan immigrant who had lived in Grand Rapids, Michigan for about seven years, died around 7:10 a.m. Sunday, September 20, 2026, after his vehicle struck a tree and caught fire near Century Avenue SW and McKendrick Street SW. Grand Rapids Police said ICE agents had attempted to stop the vehicle — registered to another Guatemalan national wanted on multiple alcohol-related driving offenses — and Coronado Juárez fled at what DHS estimated was well over 100 mph before crashing; he was pronounced dead at the scene. DHS said ICE officers 'immediately discontinued the enforcement action' for public safety and were roughly half a mile away when the crash occurred, then attempted to render aid and extinguish the fire. GRPD, which requested Michigan State Police assistance because it could not independently obtain information from federal agents, disclosed two days later that ICE had attempted the stop — an account at odds with DHS's initial framing. Governor Gretchen Whitmer directed Michigan State Police to conduct an independent review, and Grand Rapids Mayor David LaGrand denounced federal immigration officials for 'creating a culture of fear' and called for ICE reforms. Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-MI) sent a letter demanding ICE Acting Director David Venturella disclose whether agents pursued Coronado Juárez, whether body and dash cameras were activated, and whether local police were notified in advance. A community vigil was held at the crash site on Thursday, September 24, with advocacy groups GR Rapid Response to ICE and Cosecha Grand Rapids demanding transparency and renewed passage of a local sanctuary ordinance barring GRPD-ICE cooperation.
